$\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \Delta u + f(u)$

$f(u) = \lambda u + \mu u^p$

$\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \Delta u + f(u) + g(u)$

in a bounded domain $\Omega$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n \geq 2$. The nonlinearity $f$ is assumed to be of the form

$f(u) = \lambda u + \mu u^p$

where $\lambda, \mu > 0$ and $p > 1$. The nonlinearity $g$ is assumed to be of the form

$g(u) = \alpha u^q$

where $\alpha > 0$ and $q > 1$.

## Thesis

Thesis (Ph.D.)--University of Stellenbosch, 2012.

## Abstract

The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of a single bout of resistance training on the acute hormonal response to a subsequent bout of resistance training. The study was conducted in a laboratory setting and the participants were healthy, resistance-trained males. The participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups: a control group (CON) and an experimental group (EX). The CON group performed a single bout of resistance training (RT) on the first day of the study. The EX group performed a single bout of RT on the first day of the study and a second bout of RT on the second day of the study. The participants were tested for their maximal strength, body composition, and hormonal response to a single bout of RT on the first day of the study. The participants were then tested for their maximal strength, body composition, and hormonal response to a second bout of RT on the second day of the study. The results of the study showed that the EX group had a significantly greater increase in strength and body composition compared to the CON group. The EX group also had a significantly greater increase in testosterone and cortisol compared to the CON group. The results of the study suggest that a single bout of RT can induce a greater hormonal response to a subsequent bout of RT.
